newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MBS on hold ahead of cues from housing data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MBS on hold ahead of cues from housing data.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities were mostly unchanged to marginally firmer in thin dealing Tuesday, tracking Treasuries ahead of the next wave of U.S. home building and refinancing figures.

Market participants anticipated a pick-up in June housing starts and said they would closely monitor the refinancing and home purchase components of the latest Mortgage Bankers Association survey. Both reports were scheduled for Thursday.
Meanwhile, the National Association of Home Builders index reflecting housing activity in July was delayed by one day by bulk-mail problems and was rescheduled for Thursday.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast that housing starts rose to 1.45 million units from 1.397 million in May.
With Treasuries little changed, fears of home refinancing and faster MBS prepayments have moderated.

"You're going to see faster prepayments, no question about it," said one trader. He contended, however, that many investors were factoring in that trend and wouldn't be hurt significantly unless prepayments exceeded most expectations.
"We haven't been afraid to buy cuspy coupons -- the 8s and 8 1/2s," he said. The banks he deals with "feel they can shoulder the prepayment risk in exchange for higher yields."

The 8.00 percent and 8 1/2 percent coupons offered the highest yields available on 30-year MBS. Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA) 8.00 percent bonds, for example, yielded were quoted at 103-03/32 to yield 7.47 percent, 131 basis points above comparable Treasuries.
The 7.00 percent GNMA, a coupon more insulated from early prepayment, traded at 99-13/32 to yield 7.15 percent, or 86 basis points over Treasuries.
Fifteen-year MBS were mostly unchanged to slightly lower on Tuesday, slightly lagging surrounding maturities.
"We've been avoiding the 15-year, frankly," said the trader who deals primarily with banks. "We bought a lot of balloons and long paper. We're on the wings."
He said the 15-year "was in no-man's land" and there was greater value going shorter or longer.
Among active issues, 15-year 7-1/2 percent GNMAs were down 2/32 at 102-13/32 for a bond equivalent yield of 6.98 percent.
Five-year and seven-year balloon MBS were up 1/32 to 3/32.
At the long end, 30-year 7-1/2 percent GNMAs rose 1/32 to a 101-10/32 bid for a bond equivalent yield of 7.34 percent.
Comparable Federal National Mortgage Association securities gained 2/32 to 101-06/32, while Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp securities advanced 3/32 to 101-11/32.
Ten-year Treasury notes were unchanged at 102-21/32 to yield 6.26 percent and the 30-year Treasury bond rose 3/32 to 101 for a 6.55 percent yield.
